title: Residues and residue computation
terms: residue; coefficient of reciprocal term; simple-pole residue; higher-order-pole residue; logarithmic derivative.

The residue at an isolated singularity a is the coefficient of (z − a) in the local Laurent series.
At a simple pole, Res(f, a) = lim (z − a)f (z); for f = p/q with p, q holomorphic near a,

At a pole of order m, the residue is 1/(m − 1)! times the (m − 1)st derivative at a of (z − a) f(z).
Series multiplication is often faster for essential singularities or removable-looking quotients. A
2
residue can vanish even at a genuine pole, such as 1/z .
′
The logarithmic derivative F /F has residue m at a zero of order m and residue −m at a pole
±m
of order m: factor F = (z − a) h with h(a) ̸= 0. Also, the residue of the derivative of any
holomorphic function on a punctured disk is zero, as termwise differentiation of its Laurent
series shows.

Logarithmic differentiation gives F /F = 4/(z − a) + h /h. The second term is holo-
morphic near a because h is nonzero there. Thus the residue is the zero multiplicity four,
independently of the value or derivative of h.
